name: Dr. Vikram Patel
profile_summary: Dr. Vikram Patel is an Associate Professor in the Department of Information Technology, specialized in the design and runtime management of distributed Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, hardware-efficient Edge AI acceleration, and scalable Cloud Computing infrastructures. His research addresses the challenges of high latency and severe bandwidth limitations in modern sensor networks by orchestrating hybrid edge-cloud offloading pipelines. Dr. Patel's Distributed Systems Lab develops smart compilation routines and lightweight neural quantization paradigms that enable resource-constrained microcontrollers to run real-time inference tasks locally. Prior to his academic career, he spent seven years as a lead system architect at a global chip manufacturing firm, where he pioneered low-power embedded processors. He frequently consults for industrial automation and smart-city engineering consortia, translating advanced academic discoveries into field-deployed smart infrastructures. Dr. Patel holds several international patents on dynamic edge scheduling techniques.

current_projects.title: SmartCityEdge: Distributed Video Analytics on Low-Power Urban Nodes
current_projects.description: Quantizing and distributing vision-based classification models over interconnected micro-sensors for urban flow control.

current_projects.title: EcoCloud: Dynamic Edge-Cloud Offloading under Grid Constraints
current_projects.description: Developing reinforcement learning schedulers to distribute workloads across local low-power edge nodes and cloud facilities dynamically.

publications.title: Quantized Edge Inference over Low-Power Wireless Microcontrollers
publications.abstract: We evaluate an 8-bit integer post-training quantization pipeline tailored for cortex-M sensor chips. Our findings indicate a 3x speedup in neural computational cycles with minimal degradation in model evaluation accuracy.

publications.title: Dynamic Container Schedulers for IoT Edge Orchestrations
publications.conference_or_journal: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
publications.abstract: We introduce a high-efficiency orchestration layer for deploying lightweight micro-containers on resource-bound edge topologies. We minimize computational latency and device battery drainage using dynamic scheduling algorithms.

publications.title: Energy-Optimal Multi-Tier Edge Cloud Offloading Heuristics
publications.abstract: This study maps computational offloading as a constrained optimization problem. We construct a multi-tiered heuristic that accounts for link bandwidth fluctuation and edge device power status.
